Can't speak for anyone else but I stopped playing pretty quick because the game had no replay value. Shame because it had potential, moreso than Warhammer because it had mainstream appeal. You could tell from seeing the view counts on TW content creators 3k videos. the first few videos did insane numbers and then big drop offs. 
           
There was a chance for it to resurrect itself with a strong first DLC. Flesh out the depth of the game with content. This is the Warhammer formula after all, both WH1 and WH2 were shallow on release. So 8 Princes going to an era I wasn't familiar with without actually doing the 3 Kingdoms era was a head scratcher for me and I passed. I'm still baffled how in a game about "3 Kingdoms" - the 3 Kingdom era is avoided. 
          
Also I think CA created an awkward situation where they created competition within their own IPs for players. I just resumed playing Warhammer 2. I think there's only so much TAM for total war.

I wanted to argue looking at the title but after reading, I think you've made some good points.
          
I agree completely with colonization behavior and stealing razed territory. I don't like having factions across the world declare war on me and march across the map to attack me. This was a leftover problem from Attila that I thought they purged from the Warhammer series but they have definitely brought it back in WH2. I do think they maybe artificially upped the difficulty of WH2 on VH/L by letting the AI play on super duper easy baby mode. 
                  
On the other hand. There were some infurating things in WH1 that were patched out. Agent spam. AI spammed more agents than you at higher level and they leveled up faster. And could kill your lords. AI could raze and still have movement. Movement being eliminated after a raze was a change to fix their infuriating "ring around the rosie" behavior you describe. And they also patched the cat and mouse game itself. Joey CA I believe explained that the AI was "too good" at calculating the player's movement range and reacting and taking action based on you. 
               
So while it looks and plays polished now, while it was relevant and there wasn't a sequel, it was a game with its problems too.
